title: Leaking buses, bad jumps and driving accidents
summary: He rested a month before Barnet; he describes long jumps, Russell Bowles's accident, and Chu Berry's death.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: When you left Lunceford (inaudible) band? did you go directly into Charlie Barnet's

No, I -- I rested for a month or two, you know. Barnet wanted me to go directly in, but I didn't do it. I was tired, just worn out, you know. We were full of cold from leaking buses out there in the winter and freezing
in the buses, rain, had to move over that the rain don't get on you, you know.
Did Jimmie Lunceford ride the bus with the rest of the band?
Sometimes he did. Sometimes he drove his car. And the guys who had decent cars, they would drive their cars. It was kind of hard on the bus, was kind of rough.
Did Lunceford have to drive himself, or did he have somebody to drive it?
He'd drive his car. He had a big Cadillac, drive it up and down the road. But when we had the real bad jumps, he'd ride the bus -- real hard jump.
How long a jump was a bad jump?

Oh, about four, 500 miles, and you were riding from the time you left the job the night before until not too much time before you went on the next job. They didn't have the freeways like they have today where you can make good time, and it was hard. It was very hard.
If you were driving your own car, it would have meant no sleep at all, right? Or very little --

Very little, yeah. For the big jumps -- yeah, it was tough. These were tough days on the road. I know once one of the other trombone players, Russell Bowles, was driving his car, and he had an accident. He hit a guy on

a motorcycle. We were going to Buffalo, and we were already in town, and he hadn't shown up. And the guy died. He -- I don't know who was right or wrong. The guy died, and he had to go to court several times about this thing. He finally got out of it, but you're tired, you know. You play a job, and you're riding, and you're tired. It's very dangerous.

In fact, several guys got killed, like Chu Berry got killed like that, riding in a car. I think -- I think Charlie Shavers was driving that car when this happened to Chu Berry. I'm not sure. I think he was. But anyway, after work, and they're tired, you know; been quite a few accidents happened out there like that.

It was real rough. You know, you play all night, and you're worn out. So you get a bite to eat, and that makes you groggy already. You're sleep, and maybe you had a couple drinks during the night, and you're trying to drive to beat the band and get to the next town to get a few hours' sleep before the job.
And this is what guys had to -- we all had to go through at that period of time.
